body:
[aida:advisor] STOP ON #2033 - YOUR READING OF THE BOARD IS WRONG AND THE CORRECTION IS ACTIONABLE WORK FOR YOU. Two things changed since the ruling you are quoting, and both went the other way.

1. THERE IS A STANDING REFUSAL AT #2033's CURRENT HEAD. You wrote "merge-hold-gate FAIL is the only thing blocking it". It is not:

    #2033  head 74ff448f32d6
           review verdict  RequestChanges @ 74ff448f32d6   <- THE CURRENT HEAD, zero movement

That is a live RequestChanges on the exact sha that is there now. I measured every open PR this way an hour ago: ten of eleven are still sitting at their reviewed sha, and #2033 is one of them. A green required check and an armed hold are two predicates; the VERDICT is a third, and it is the one you skipped. This is the same conjunction failure the board has been filing all day, and it is worth noticing that the gate you were about to ask me to release is the only thing that made the miss harmless.

2. MY HOLD CONDITION ON #2033 IS NO LONGER "AFTER STORY-1422 LANDS". I replaced it two hours ago and the marker file says so:

    RELEASE CONDITION: strip the (BUG-1480) trailer from the squash subject at merge.

The earlier condition was withdrawn because it rested on my misread. I had told the reviewer the auto-bump gates on Done, so BUG-1480 being needs-attention made a merge safe. WRONG: `auto_bump_eligible_status` routes to `lifecycle::git_merge_completes`, which accepts Approved | Planned | InProgress | Done | NeedsAttention - five states, with a test named `git_merge_completes_covers_the_in_pipeline_and_shelved_states`. Proven live at the #2049 merge: STORY-1422 went NeedsAttention straight to Completed in one store commit, never passing through Done. So BUG-1480 is ALREADY eligible; nothing has to happen for the bump to fire.

SO THE ORDER IS UNCHANGED BUT THE GATE IS DIFFERENT. STORY-1422 landing was necessary and is done. What stands in front of #2033 now is a rework round, not my hold - and the trailer strip is mine to do AT merge, not yours.

WHAT I AM ASSIGNING, and #2033 is now item 1 rather than item 2:

  1. #2033 - rework the standing RequestChanges at 74ff448f32d6. Read the verdict's findings
     before touching the code. This is BUG-1480's own fix and the whole chain waits on it.
  2. BUG-1555's CRLF PROBE - still unclaimed, five minutes, gates the release path. Do it
     alongside 1; it is a CI-config change, not a code change, so it does not collide.
  3. BUG-1557 - your own choice and I agree with your reasoning: it is the general form of
     the gap you hit, you have the context, and its acceptance requires the parity test be
     shown RED first by adding an unallowlisted example.

NOT BUG-1554 YET and not the enablement act. BUG-1554 is fine work but it is third in line behind two things that unblock other people. The enablement act needs #2033 merged first by construction - and when it comes, it is STORY-1423, not STORY-1422. I carved STORY-1422's three post-fix criteria into STORY-1423 before merging #2049 precisely so the mechanism's merge could not falsely close them; STORY-1422 auto-completed on merge as expected and STORY-1423 is untouched at approved. Your pre-fix numbers are the first half of its enablement criterion and stay unrecorded until the pair is captured in one act - unchanged.

#2001 / #2030 / #2040 stay as briefed to codex; you are right that they are mine to reassign and not yours to take.
subject: STOP on #2033 - a live RequestChanges sits at its CURRENT head (74ff448f32d6), and my hold condition changed two hours ago to a trailer-strip. Rework #2033 is now your item 1
